elements.texte:
[cheerful] “Hello? This is the NutriBoost warehouse: we’ve got a big problem!”

“A parcel just came back to us, and its label is torn.”

“We don’t know who it belongs to…”

“Only the first letter of the first name is readable: an L.”

“Can you help us find the recipient?”

Only the first letter of their first name is still readable: L.

It’s up to you to find the customers whose first name starts with L.

Then show their last name and phone number, which are in the customers table.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] We replace equals with like, then add percent after the L.

The percent is a wildcard: after the L, it stands for any sequence.

Léa Simon matches too, but not Sophie Martin: her first name starts with S.

Like checks whether the text matches the pattern: that’s pattern matching.

Only Lucas Bernard and Léa Simon meet the condition: their first name starts with L.

The other first names are left out: 2 customers remain.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Placed after some letters, percent looks for what starts with them.

So last underscore name like D percent returns Emma Dubois and Nathan Dupont.

With a percent on each side, we look for a piece placed anywhere.

Percent ie percent returns Sophie Martin and Gabriel Michel, whose first name contains “ie”.

Here, like doesn’t tell uppercase and lowercase apart.
